intelligence.essence: Proof and permission are two axes, and merging them is the defect: a fully green tip withholds deployment until the director's explicit dispatch (SN-0441), a 9.8/10 scorecard still returns DENY on a protected path (SN-0523), a scorecard decides what should happen but never permits who may do it (SN-0565), and an authorization is a (sha, scope, window) triple that lapses the moment the tip moves (SN-0475). Authority is human-rooted, scope-exact, and verified at action time — a self-declared grant is a claim (SN-0444), a name on a form is not an entitlement (SN-0464), and an author string is not provenance (SN-0409).
intelligence.human_view: This is the block's governance spine: the long, careful separation between "we proved it" and "we may do it." Every failure here is a version of the same confusion — a green check treated as permission, a name treated as an entitlement, a document granting itself authority, a score treated as a signature. And every success is the separation held under pressure: at the greenest moment, at the highest score, with the director's own conditional words available as an excuse. The envelope held because the axes never merged.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a clubhouse with two different locks. One lock is the scoreboard: it says how well you did on the quiz. The other lock is the permission slip: it says whether Mom said you may go. Winning the quiz doesn't open the permission lock — only Mom's actual words do. A note you wrote yourself saying "Mom said yes" is not Mom saying yes. And her yes was for Tuesday's trip: if the trip changes, you need a new yes. Scores are real, and permissions are real — they're just different things.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it's the difference between the bank saying your check is good and the bank being allowed to cash it — both matter, and neither substitutes for the other. A signature line filled with any name at all is not an authorization; a glowing inspection report is not a building permit; and a permit for the old blueprints doesn't cover the new ones. The team's discipline is the clerk's discipline: check who actually granted it, what exactly it covers, and whether it's still the same job it was granted for.
intelligence.ai_view: On every consequential action: compute readiness and permission as separate outputs, permission second and independent (SN-0523, SN-0565); trace authority to its human root — the director's word, a ratified standing law, or an ACTIVE grant with scope and expiry (SN-0565); refuse self-declared grants and author-string provenance (SN-0444, SN-0409); bind promoters to the entitlement roster, never to a non-blank string (SN-0362, SN-0464); treat every authorization as a (sha, scope, window) triple and re-anchor before the window (SN-0475, SN-0574); replay the selection behind any receipt that drives an authority decision (SN-0556); forge coherently when you test a gate (SN-559); re-derive the classification at action time instead of trusting the narrative (SN-560); and classify a deny by scope before touching any matcher (SN-0566).
intelligence.what_it_means: Fourteen notes draw one bright line through everything the fleet does: evidence flows upward freely, authority flows from the human root only, and no mechanism — score, retrieval, learning, narrative, or self-declaration — mints permission. A cold reader holding only this essence can audit any "authorized" claim in the system and find either its human root or its defect.
whats_inside: Two axes, always separate outputs: proven (score/CI) and permitted (authority) (SN-0441, SN-0523, SN-0565).
A grant comes from the director's explicit word, never from the artifact's own text, an author string, or a score (SN-0444, SN-0409, SN-0565).
Entitlement is a binding to a roster, scoped to the act — never a non-blank name (SN-0362, SN-0464).
Promotion is atomic with the pointer moving last; failure before the pointer means the pointer never moves (SN-0363).
Authorization is a (sha, scope, window) triple; it lapses when the tip moves; a failed dispatch is stale production, not partial progress (SN-0475, SN-0574).
Validate the selection, not just the artifact: replay canonical selection at the receipt's pinned inputs (SN-0556); test gates with coherent forgeries, not garbage (SN-559).
Re-derive the authority classification at action time; stale narrative loses to ratified law (SN-560).
A fail-closed deny on an out-of-scope target is the system working; widen scope only by a new human grant, never by loosening the matcher (SN-0566).
